newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Malaysian firms line up for Australia's Docklands.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian firms line up for Australia's Docklands.

text.p: Malaysian developers on Wednesday emerged as strong bidders for the right to redevelop Melbourne's waterfront.
Seven Malaysian companies feature in the 12 consortiums that were declared bidders for the A$2.5 billion inner-city Docklands project by the Victoria state government's Docklands Authority.
Some of the biggest names in Australian property are also vying for one or more of the project's five precincts, according to a statement issued by the authority on Wednesday.
The all-Australian Melbourne Docklands consortium, comprising Hudson Conway Ltd, Lend Lease Corp Ltd and Mirvac Ltd group, has bid for all five precincts.
Hudson Conway has said in the past that it and Lend Lease want to win the rights to all five precincts, or none at all.
The authority said on Wednesday it expected to choose two preferred bidders for each precinct by August and recommend them to the state government for a final decision.
- Gasing Heights Sdn Bhd, in association with Swinburne University
- Tech 2000 consortium, including BZW Australia Ltd
- YarraCity consortium, including Thiess Contractors, McIntosh Corporate, Austral Amalgamated Bhd, IJM Corp Bhd and Land and General Bhd
- APAC International consortium, including Jeram Kuantan (Malaya) Bhd and Tanco Properties Sdn Bhd
- Entertainment City consortium, including Macquarie Bank Ltd
- Yarranova consortium, comprises virtually the same team as YarraCity consortium
- Australian Property Network Pty Ltd, including Grocon Pty Ltd
- Victoria Harbour Corp, including KPMG, Fletcher Constructions and the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd
